description:
FILED s516b (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-12) from the #3241 re-bless (these files used to read PASS 1/0).

REPRODUCE:  tools/run-dist-t.pl ~/.cpan/build/Capture-Tiny-0.50-0 t/20-stdout-badtie.t   (ok 1, then "unimplemented" from a top-level form, rc 2)
perl:       cd ~/.cpan/build/Capture-Tiny-0.50-0 && perl -Ilib t/20-stdout-badtie.t    (583 rows)
Same in 21-stderr-badtie.t, 22-stdin-badtie.t, 24-all-badtied.t.

The file: `tie *STDOUT, 'TieEvil'; ok(tied *STDOUT, ...); my $fd = next_fd; run_test(...)` -- t/lib/TieEvil.pm's methods die "unimplemented".  NOT the TAP layer writing through the tie: a minimal `tie *STDOUT, 'Evil'; ok(1); ok(1)` with a dying PRINT passes under PCL (scratch/s516b/pr/tie1.pl).  So some later step (t/lib/Utils.pm next_fd's open/dup of STDOUT, or Capture::Tiny's own save/restore) calls a tied method -- OPEN / FILENO / BINMODE -- that perl's real handle operation does not.  Next step: bisect the file's statements after row 1 with a print before each.
subject: Capture-Tiny's four *badtie* files: after `tie *STDOUT, 'TieEvil'` (a class whose methods die "unimplemented") the program dies after row 1 (SBCL rc 2) where perl runs 583 rows -- PCL calls a tied-handle method perl never reaches
